scripts.//verify: Shared gate. Everything MUST be built before linting: type-aware lint resolves workspace imports through each package's dist/*.d.mts, and it also covers examples/ — which need @zintl-examples/* dists and vinext's generated .next types. On a fresh checkout, linting first yields ~172 phantom 'Cannot find module' errors.
scripts.verify: vpr build:examples && vp lint && knip && vp test && vp fmt --check
scripts.//ready: verify plus the perf gate. The bench runs SECOND, right after the package build and before everything heavy, because it measures latency and the machine it measures is the one the previous step left behind: run last, after 27 example builds, type-aware lint and 800 tests, the same benchmark reads 3.4ms where it reads 0.5ms here. Budgets are relative and absorb a uniformly slower machine, but nothing absorbs measuring during the cooldown of a job that just saturated the box.
scripts.ready: vpr build && vp run bench && vpr build:examples && vp lint && knip && vp test && vp fmt
scripts.//browsers: The browsers `test:contracts` drives. A script rather than an inline CI command on purpose: knip resolves the root's `@playwright/test` through this script, and CI runs the same line you would.
scripts.//smoke: Outside-in publish gate: packs the real tarballs, installs them with npm into a throwaway app outside this workspace, and builds against stock Vite and stock Rsbuild. Every published entry point gets a run. Needs network. Run before releasing.
scripts.//flake: Run one contract N times and report failures/N. Use it before AND after any change to an intermittent contract, in the same sitting: a single run of a flaky test carries almost no information, and a baseline measured an hour earlier carries less. It builds first and refuses to run against a stale dist.
scripts.//version-packages: Formats after versioning because the two tools disagree about Markdown. Changesets writes CHANGELOG entries with trailing spaces on the blank lines inside a list item; oxfmt strips them. Nobody edits those files by hand, so the disagreement only ever surfaces as `vp fmt --check` failing on the version PR — a red gate on a PR whose whole content is generated. Formatting here means the PR is born passing.
